title: Microfabricated Platforms for Mechanically Dynamic Cell Culture
protocol: Fabricate single- or multi-level SU-8 masters in a cleanroom using standard procedures for the pneumatic microactuator array.
Hard bake the masters at 80 °C for three days prior to use.
Clean glass slides in a vacuum chamber.
Pipette 60 μL of tridecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetrahydrooctyl-1-trichlorosilane into a petri dish in the vacuum chamber.
Place bare glass and SU-8 masters in the vacuum chamber.
Maintain under vacuum overnight for silanization.
Cut two foam pads to sizes slightly larger than the SU-8 master.
Cut an overhead inkjet transparency film to sizes slightly larger than the SU-8 master.
Mix PDMS monomer and crosslinker in a 10:1 ratio thoroughly.
Deposit 3 mL of uncured PDMS mixture onto a previously fabricated SU-8 master.
Degas the PDMS mixture in a vacuum chamber.
Place the foam pad and SU-8 master on a plexiglass base plate.
Lower the transparency carefully onto the uncured PDMS, ensuring no air bubbles are trapped.
Ensure that the smooth side of the transparency contacts the uncured PDMS.
Place a silanized glass slide on top of the transparency beneath the second foam pad.
Position a plexiglass top plate over the setup.
Clamp the sandwich together using a C-clamp.
Cure the PDMS sandwich in an oven at 80 °C for at least 4 hours.
Remove the cured sandwich from the oven and allow it to cool before removing the clamp.
Discard the foam pads after removing the clamp.
Peel away the transparency carefully, retaining the patterned PDMS film.
Store the patterned PDMS layers and handling transparencies in a dust-free environment until needed.
Transfer the PDMS layer to a clean glass slide.
Treat the PDMS and glass surfaces with oxygen plasma using a corona discharge unit.
Place the treated PDMS and glass surfaces in contact with each other.
Place the stack on a hotplate at 80 °C to complete the bonding process.
Peel away and discard the transparency.
Remove any thin films of PDMS that have not been squeezed out from between the SU-8 features and the transparency manually using a 25G needle under a stereoscope if necessary.
Silanize the negative replica mold formed as a second sandwich molded layer.
Temporarily affix the silanized negative replica mold to a glass slide using double-sided tape.
Deposit uncured PDMS onto this sandwich mold layer.
Degass the deposited PDMS.
Spin-coat the degassed PDMS for 45 seconds at 1000 RPM, yielding an actuation diaphragm 60 μm thick.
Partially cure the spin-coated PDMS layer at 80 °C for approximately 20 minutes, or until the PDMS is sticky but does not deform permanently when touched.
Remove glass slide and double-sided tape from partially-cured PDMS layer.
Plasma-treat the exposed surface of the PDMS layer.
Invert the plasma-treated PDMS layer and place it in a custom-made aligner.
Place the first PDMS layer on a rotary stage beneath the vacuum chuck.
Observe alignment between the two layers using a Navitar 12x zoom machine vision system.
Align the layers using the manipulator.
Carefully bring the aligned layers into contact.
Remove the sandwich from the aligner and cure in an oven at 80 °C for 30 minutes.
Peel the transparency and silanized replica PDMS mold from the device and discard it.
Fully cure the device at 80 °C for at least four hours.
Use a needle to clear the PDMS layer at the point of connection.
Cast approximately 35 g of PDMS in an omni-well tray.
Cure the casted PDMS and peel it out.
Cut the cured PDMS into small gasket sections.
Remove a 1/8" hole from each section using a punch.
Use an 18G blunted needle to core out a section from the side of the gasket.
With a smaller 21G needle, remove the central core before withdrawing the 18G needle.
Cast approximately 15g of PDMS in an omni-well tray lid.
Cure and peel this casted PDMS.
Cut it into similarly sized sections as previously prepared.
Clean each section with scotch tape.
Plasma-bond these cleaned sections to the top of the gasket.
Bond the unit, punched side down, onto the device using plasma bonding.
Separate a blunt 18G needle from the colored plastic luer connector.
Insert this separated needle into the cored hole in the gasket and seal it with a few drops of PDMS.
Bond a third PDMS layer to the device, as shown in Figure 3a.
Spin coat a 10-15 μm thick layer of PDMS onto the smooth side of a transparency (spin parameters: 4000 RPM, 120 seconds).
Cure the coated PDMS at 80 °C for at least 4 hours.
Apply a low-level vacuum to the actuators, lowering the array of posts.
Plasma treat and bond the spin coated PDMS film to the actuated microdevice.
Place the bonded device on a hotplate at 80 °C for 10 minutes.
Fill the lubrication channels with a 90% glycerol in deionized water solution.
Place the device on a hotplate at 40 °C.
Inject lubricant into the channel, causing a small pressure increase.
Continue until air bubbles diffuse through the PDMS.
Remove the negative pressure, releasing the posts.
Cut around the thin PDMS film using a scalpel.
Carefully peel the transparency backing away from the device.
Plasma bond a hand-cut PDMS gasket around the device culture area.
Sterilize the device by soaking in 70% ethanol for 5 minutes.
Place the sterilized device under germicidal UV light for 45 minutes.
Plasma treat the surface of the device.
Incubate the treated surface with 100 μg/mL collagen overnight at 4 °C.
Wash the device with phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Seed cells at 10-15000 cells/cm2, following standard cell culture protocols.
Coat posts with a 1 μm thick layer of Parylene-C to reduce gas permeability and improve polymerization times.
Mask areas around the post using pieces of scotch tape.
Place the device in a PDS 2010 LabCoter 2 system for coating.
Remove the coated device from the coating system.
Peel away the scotch tape, leaving a conformal layer of Parylene-C over the posts.
Methacrylate a glass coverslip by immersing it in a 2% v/v solution of 3-(trimethoxysilyl) propyl methacrylate in 95% ethanol for 2 minutes.
Rinse the coverslip with 100% ethanol after removal from the methacrylation solution.
Bake the coverslip at 100 °C to leave methacrylate groups on the surface.
Cast a 200 μm thick PDMS spacer film in a petri dish.
Cut the PDMS spacer film into small sections.
Plasma bond four small sections around the edge of the methacrylated coverslip.
Plasma bond the spacers to the PDMS-areas of the device, covering Parylene-C coated posts.
Sterilize the device by washing in 70% ethanol.
Expose the device to germicidal UV light for 45 minutes in a biological safety cabinet.
Prepare a 10% w/v PEGDA (3.4kDa) and 10% w/v PEG (8kDa) solution in unsupplemented cell culture media.
Prepare a photoinitiator stock solution of 100 mg/mL Irgacure 2959 in 1-vinyl-2-pyrolidinone.
Mix the PEGDA and PEG solution with the photoinitiator stock solution to obtain a 0.4% w/v photoinitiator concentration.
Filter the mixture through a 0.45 μm syringe filter to sterilize and remove particulates.
Trpysinize cell cultures and prepare a cell suspension in culture media at twice the desired end-point cell concentration.
Mix the cell suspension with the filtered hydrogel precursor/photoinitiator solution in a 1:1 ratio.
Inject the solution into the microdevice using a long 25G needle, carefully avoiding trapping bubbles.
Align a printed transparency mask to alignment marks on the device surface.
Set up a UV illumination system to provide a UV dose of 17.5 mW/cm2 at the device surface.
Illuminate the hydrogel through the mask for 195 s.
Wash away unpolymerized hydrogel precursor solution with PBS.
Replace the PBS with culture media.
Actuate the loading posts to compress the hydrogel constructs.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl with human recombinant leptin.
Use modified petri dishes for maintaining sterility during actuation of devices.
Epoxy a blunted and stripped 18G needle into the side of the petri dish.
Fit tubing to the connectors and connect it to controlled solenoid valves and pressure sources.
Generate positive pressures from 30-55 kPa using an eccentric diaphragm pump for 2D experiments.
Use pulse-width modulation based voltage controller to vary applied voltage for controlling pressure output.
Actuate solenoid valves with a 12 V signal, controlled by a square waveform function generator.
Resolve condensation issues beneath PDMS film supporting loading post by addressing temperature and humidity differences.
Connect an open reservoir to the pressure inlet port.
Fill the reservoir with deionized water.
Place the device and filled reservoir in a vacuum chamber.
Pump down the chamber.
Wait 5 minutes.
Bring the chamber to atmospheric pressure.
Repeat two or three times.
Image culture areas using bright field or fluorescence microscopy.
Dilute 1 μm diameter fluorescent beads in methanol to the desired concentration.
Plasma treat the device surface.
Deposit 5-10 μL of bead suspension on the treated surface.
Wait for the methanol to evaporate.
Repeat if bead concentration is too low.
Image the cell culture areas at rest, and under load.
Mix a quantity of fluorescent beads into the hydrogel precursor solution.
Image the system using a confocal microscope.
Track bead displacements in the imaged system.
Analyze and fit bead displacement data to a deformation model.
